S057-01.notes: 'does not diminish ... rather, she relocates it' -- the rather-clause keeps the achievement and moves the credit, which only fits diminish. D (romanticize) is the strongest trap because earlier accounts did romanticize individual genius, but 'does not romanticize the achievement; rather relocates it' is not a logical contrast. B and C reverse or miss the logic.

S057-02.notes: Pattern (urban patenting), a common explanation (face-to-face contact), an alternative (sorting), and a relocation study that tells the two apart. A and B wrongly say the passage finds a flaw. D wrongly says the two are supported equally, but the study rules out sorting alone.

S057-03.notes: Neither approach escapes the problem: one loses ambiguity, the other loses ease. A favors fragmentary versions, which the critic rejects. C is unsupported. D overstates 'must lose something' as 'cannot be translated' and adds a recommendation the text never makes.

flags.note: Simplifies Winawer et al. (2007): the reported result was a category advantage. Russian speakers were faster at cross-boundary than within-category discriminations, while English speakers showed no such effect. The study did not report Russian speakers being faster than English speakers outright. Verbal interference (rehearsing a digit string) removed the advantage and spatial interference did not, so the item stays accurate. Consider rewording to 'Russian speakers, unlike English speakers, were faster at telling apart blues that fell on opposite sides of that boundary than blues on the same side'. The phrase 'through the words people use in the moment' is also slightly awkward.

S057-04.notes: The advantage disappears under verbal interference, so language affects the speed of perception online and does not determine what speakers can see. A misreads 'faster' as 'could not see'. B overreaches because the researchers say language can influence perception. C has no support.

S057-05.notes: Checked the text against the Johnson version: the lines and dashes match, though stanza breaks are omitted, which is acceptable. 'Around 1861' is acceptable (Johnson dates it about 1861; Franklin dates it 1862). Only C covers both halves of the claim, harsh conditions ('Extremity') and demanding nothing ('never... asked a crumb'). B covers harsh conditions only, A covers persistence only, and D covers the storm and warmth but not demanding nothing.

S057-06.notes: Arithmetic checks out: +4k, +4k, then +27k. Only A sets the prior trend against the jump. D compares growth after the jump (2020-21), which says nothing about the 2019-20 break. B and C are true but irrelevant.

S057-07.notes: Dangling modifier: the person who analyzed the recordings must be the subject, which is 'the team'. A, C and D all leave the modifier dangling.

S057-08.notes: 'By the time [past event]' plus 'for more than a decade' requires the past perfect progressive. C (was directing) is the main trap but does not fit 'by the time... for more than a decade'. Facts check out: Roebling was disabled by caisson disease around 1872, directed the work from his Brooklyn Heights room overlooking the river, and the bridge opened in 1883.
